basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models the verifier-side binding of a statement, proof and result, not the credential or key it relies on.
Records only the class of private inputs and never stores the witness itself.
Keeps cryptographic validity, issuer trust, status and business acceptance as separate outcomes.
Qualifies privacy properties by named proof system, version and threat model.

may: Create a verification request with a fresh challenge and audience.
Verify a proof with the declared verification material and record the result.
Assess a disclosure manifest against the stated predicate.
Re-evaluate results when a proof system or key is later found weak.
mustNot: Persist a witness, holder secret or undisclosed claim.
Treat a valid proof as authorization or eligibility on its own.
Claim zero knowledge or unlinkability without naming the system and assumptions.
Request more attributes than the predicate needs.
Accept a presentation bound to a different challenge or audience.
requiresHuman: Choosing or approving a proof system and its trusted setup.
Accepting a verification result for a high-stakes decision such as age or eligibility gates.

considerations: Zero-knowledge checks exist to protect privacy; over-requesting or logging undermines that purpose.
Verifiers can track people by correlating proofs; unlinkability needs design, not assumption.
People without suitable devices or credentials may be excluded from services.

items: A verification record has a statement or predicate, a challenge, a proof reference, a proof-system profile and a result.
It is confused with the credential, a digital signature check or an authorization decision.
Replay of a proof when challenge binding is missing.
Unsound circuits or setups that accept false statements.
Correlation of holders through reused identifiers in proofs.
